articles.title: Trump says he has set no deadline for Ukraine-Russia peace deal
articles.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said he had set no deadline for reaching a peace deal between Ukraine and Russia, saying he hoped the war would end as soon as possible. — Ukrinform.

articles.title: Trump Freezes Russia Business Deals as Ukraine Peace Talks Return to Territory and Security
articles.description: Washington shelves plans for economic cooperation with Moscow, including energy investments and potential Nord Stream deals, as negotiations shift back towards territorial concessions and security guarantees. articles.title: A Russian strike on Ukraine kills 2 and wounds 48 as Kyiv explains its attack in Libya
articles.description: Russia and Ukraine have escalated their aerial strikes in recent months even as they engage in US-mediated talks to end the war.

articles.title: Zelensky outlines what could force Russia to agree to a ceasefire
articles.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky said that the resilience and unity of Ukraine’s partners – the United States and Europe – combined with Russia’s heavy battlefield losses and mounting economic costs, would eventually force Moscow to agree to a ceasefire. — Ukrinform.

articles.title: The Russia-Ukraine War’s Dangerous Divergence
articles.description: Perspective: Peace talks gather pace even as the fighting spreads from the Baltic to the Mediterranean. That's no contradiction.

articles.title: Pentagon Holds Up Approval For 60 Patriot Missiles For Ukraine. Kyiv Fears US Pressure Over Peace Deal: Report
articles.description: Ukraine's Western allies are financing the weapons as Russia intensifies attacks on Ukrainian cities and critical infrastructure ahead of winter.

articles.title: Russia's Medvedev warns of potential nuclear strike amid ongoing Ukraine conflict
articles.description: Russia has indicated the potential for a preventive nuclear attack under specific conditions in the ongoing Ukraine conflict. Dmitry Medvedev stated that the decision would ultimately lie with President Vladimir Putin. Additionally, recent reports suggested that Moscow might be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite soon. NATO officials and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy have called for increased vigilance and negotiations.
